range.remark: Ps 80:14-18 (conclusion), Pss 81-86. Ps 87 introduction begins pdf 118, verse notes -> next batch.

entries.emendation: מִיָּעַר → מִיְּאֹר (with ל as litera suspensa)
entries.note: In חזיר מיער the ל is a litera suspensa, per talmudic evidence; the word was originally read מיאר ('from the Nile'), but to make the verse allude to the boar as symbol of Rome it was read מיער — not altered outright, but with a letter superscripted (as with נ in משה). The sense: the swine of the Nile — Egypt (יאר) — ravages the vine, Israel.
זיז שדי is not properly understood, and ירענה ('grazes it') is too weak a verb for the destruction described; leg. something stronger.
entries.flag: the proposed stronger verb is garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.mt: וְכַנָּה אֲשֶׁר־נָטְעָה יְמִינֶךָ וְעַל־בֵּן אִמַּצְתָּה לָּךְ
entries.emendation: transpose with v.17a; ועל בן → ועל בן אדם (as LXX/Pesch. at v.18)
entries.note: The second half of v.16 is very dark — בן 'shoot' is without analogy, and the preposition על (with פקד) denotes hostile treatment; moreover LXX and Peshitta read בן אדם here too, as at v.18, where the sense is decidedly hostile. If compelled to read ועל בן אדם here as well, it must be taken in malam partem — and then the abrupt v.17b (מגערת פניך יאבדו), whose subject is otherwise unclear, becomes intelligible: it can only refer to בן אדם, continuing v.16b's thought. The 'son of man' is the adversary who mistreats the vine and garden; אמצתה לך (used twice) means God strengthened this enemy to his own people's harm — he might be called איש ימינך, though better leg. איש ריבך. Both verses gain plain sense once v.17a (שרפה) is joined to v.16a and vice versa: 'ופקד גפן זאת וגנה אשר נטעה ימינך שרופה באש כסוחה, ועל בן אמצתה לך מגערת פניך יאבד'. The hostile prince is most likely Necho of Egypt, who dealt harshly with Judah after Josiah's death.
כסוחה, as Isa 5:25 (נבלתם כסוחה); supply the comparative כ, which drops before the identical letter: ככסוחה 'like a felled thorn-bush'.

'שאו זמרה' cannot properly be said in Hebrew (cf. Job 21:12 ישאו בתוף וכנור, where likewise one must read ישירו): leg. שירו 'sing' here too. And תנו is irregular — when and why would a hand-drum be 'given'? Leg. תפו תף 'beat the drum'.
עדות ביהוסף is an abstruse form; leg. עדות ביהודה ויוסף, equivalent to ביהודה וישראל or ביעקב וישראל — God appointed this feast for both halves of the nation, at the time He went out against Egypt.

entries.mt: הֲסִירוֹתִי מִסֵּבֶל שִׁכְמוֹ כַּפָּיו מִדּוּד תַּעֲבֹרְנָה
entries.note: דוד as 'basket' or 'pot' would be a tasteless image here. Pesch. more fittingly has 'from the fetters' (מן אסוריא). Vielleicht leg. מעבוד or מעבודה 'from servitude, labor'.

entries.mt: לוּ עַמִּי שֹׁמֵעַ לִי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּדְרָכַי יְהַלֵּכוּ
entries.emendation: שֹׁמֵעַ → שָׁמַע (perfect); יְהַלֵּכוּ → הָלְכוּ (perfect, the extra י dittographed)
entries.note: לו is followed by the participle שמע; leg. instead the perfect שמע, per LXX εἰ ἤκουσε and Pesch. And the י in the last word (יהלכו) is dittographed; leg. the perfect הלכו (LXX ἐπορεύθη) — all perfects throughout, conveying that it is now over, beyond redress.

entries.mt: וַיַּאֲכִילֵהוּ מֵחֵלֶב חִטָּה וּמִצּוּר דְּבַשׁ אַשְׂבִּיעֶךָ
entries.emendation: וַיַּאֲכִילֵם ... מִצּוֹף דְּבַשׁ ... יַשְׂבִּיעֵם (all third-person plural)
entries.note: LXX render throughout with third-person-plural suffixes (ἐψώμισεν αὐτούς ... ἐχόρτασεν αὐτούς); Pesch. likewise has not אשביעך but the third person שבעם: leg. ויאכילם ... ישביעם. Also emend מצור to מצוף 'from the flow [of honey]' (so Schorr and Dyserinck).

entries.mt: אֱלֹהִים נִצָּב בַּעֲדַת־אֵל בְּקֶרֶב אֱלֹהִים יִשְׁפֹּט
entries.note: בקרב אלהים is surely a corruption; perhaps originally בית ישראל (cf. Hos 10:15 ככה אעשה לכם בית אל, LXX οἶκος τοῦ Ισραηλ). The separated syllable הים should be read הוא: 'בקרב ישראל הוא ישפט' — 'in Israel's midst He judges'.
דל ותום in v.3, repeating דל again at v.4 (דל ואביון), is stylistically inadmissible; leg. תם statt יתום.

entries.mt: אָכֵן כְּאָדָם תְּמוּתוּן וּכְאַחַד הַשָּׂרִים תִּפֹּלוּ
entries.note: כאדם fittingly means obscure people without family standing. But וכאחד השרים ('like one of the princes') is untenable; leg. instead a phrase meaning 'like one of the lowly ones' (הצעירים).

entries.mt: קוּמָה אֱלֹהִים שָׁפְטָה הָאָרֶץ כִּי־אַתָּה תִנְחַל בְּכָל־הַגּוֹיִם
entries.note: כי אתה תנחל is not properly intelligible; leg. תמשל 'for Thou dost rule over all the nations'.

אשור is probably a corruption of גשור; Pesch. has גשור for האשורי at 2 Sam 2:9, and Gen 25:18's באכה אשורה (of Ishmael's descendants) likely also equals גשורה — they can hardly have reached Assyria proper. The Geshurites of the northern Hauran border fit both the geography and Judas Maccabeus's campaigns (Karnaim, Bosra) far better than true Assyria.
En-Dor is nowhere else mentioned as a battle site; it is probably a miswriting for עין חרד, where Gideon encamped and struck the Midianites (Judg 7:1).
'Heart and flesh sing' cannot be right — heart and body can rejoice, but not sing or cry aloud. Leg. יכלו or יכספו, 'long, yearn for'.

entries.mt: גַּם־צִפּוֹר מָצְאָה בַיִת וּדְרוֹר קֵן לָהּ ... אֶת־מִזְבְּחוֹתֶיךָ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
entries.emendation: supply הַרְאֵנִי (or רְאֵה) before את מזבחותיך
entries.note: A gap is presupposed before את מזבחותיך (Judah Ibn-Balam ad loc., cited by Ibn Ezra); supply a verb such as ראה or הראני, as 1 Sam 15:25 (הראני את...).

entries.mt: אַשְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵי בֵיתֶךָ עוֹד יְהַלְלוּךָ סֶּלָה
entries.note: עוד יהללוך can mean neither 'still/future' nor 'constantly' fittingly here; LXX's rendering (εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων) guessed at עד עולם ועד, which doesn't even suit. Leg. סוד (confusion of ע/ס), turning יהללוך into the noun מהלליך: 'סוד מהלליך' — the circle of the Levites, elsewhere called קראי שמו (Ps 99:6).

entries.mt: אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם עוֹז־לוֹ בָךְ מְסִלּוֹת בִּלְבָבָם
entries.emendation: עוֹז־לוֹ → מְעוּזוֹ; מְסִלּוֹת בִּלְבָבָם → הָלֹךְ בָּם מְסִלּוֹת(?)
entries.note: אשרי אדם forms a contrast with ישבי ביתך (v.5) — those who do not dwell in the Temple but visit it from time to time. עז לו leg. מעוזו (the מ absorbed). And מסלות בלבבם is untenable — neither מעלות (ס/ע confusion, LXX ἀναβάσεις) nor Hupfeld's forced כסלות 'hope' works; in any case the plural בלבבם is incongruent with the singular עז — leg. a phrase such as 'הלך בם' along the lines of 'the highways [to Zion] are in their heart'.

entries.emendation: עֵמֶק הַבָּכָא → עֵמֶק הַבְּכָאִים (מ absorbed by the following מעין)
entries.note: עמק הבכא is a proper name (Kimchi, Gesenius, Olshausen), more properly עמק הבכאים, the מ absorbed by the following מעין — a locality where the בכא-shrub (a balsam) grew, in the Valley of Rephaim (2 Sam 5:23), sparsely fruitful per Isa 17:5; עמק רפאים and עמק הבכאים appear to be nearly identical places.

ברכות here means 'blessings' in the sense of fruitfulness (as ברכות שדים); more properly it would be בְּרֵכוֹת 'pools', but that does not suit מורה. Leg. יעטהו (referring back to עמק); מורה = יורה 'the early rain'.

entries.mt: יֵלְכוּ מֵחַיִל אֶל־חָיִל יֵרָאֶה אֶל־אֱלֹהִים בְּצִיּוֹן
entries.emendation: יֵלְכוּ לְהֵיכַל אֵל חַי לֵרָאֹת אֶל־אֱלֹהִים בְּצִיּוֹן
entries.note: מחיל אל חיל יראה makes no sense. Necessarily leg. להיכל אל חי, joining the ל of the second חיל with יראה to give the Niphal infinitive לראה. LXX confirm at the close not just אלהים בציון but אל אלהים, ὀφθήσεται ὁ θεὸς τῶν θεῶν — so the original read ילכו להיכל אל חי לראה(ת) אל אלהים בציון. The deliberate euphemistic change made the verb passive ('be seen') rather than active ('see') where God is the object — a tiqqun soferim. Through fusion of חי with the following ל, only חיל remained.

entries.mt: מָגִנֵּנוּ רְאֵה אֱלֹהִים וְהַבֵּט פְּנֵי מְשִׁיחֶךָ
entries.note: מגננו cannot be vocative — that disturbs the parallelism's symmetry — but must mean 'protector, prince' (cf. Ps 47:10). The verse makes sense once read as the plural משיחיך, 'anointed, favored ones' (as Ps 105:15 אל תגעו במשיחי), probably referring to priests here; accordingly one must also read the plural in a., מגננו 'our protectors'.
The old versions still preserve אחד with טוב (ἡμέραν μίαν, 'one day'); אחד was displaced by the following אלף.

entries.mt: כִּי שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה׳ אֱלֹהִים חֵן וְכָבוֹד יִתֵּן ה׳ לֹא יִמְנַע־טוֹב
entries.emendation: draw אלהים into the second clause (with LXX)
entries.note: כי שמש ומגן is an unfitting image if שמש means 'sun' — an aggadic reading (Rashi; Midrash Tehillim) rightly takes שמש as 'city-wall battlement' instead (cf. Arabic šams also denoting a comb's radiating teeth), giving both this verse and Isa 54:12 a far better sense. Separately, LXX oddly render חן ואמת אהב ה' — more likely they draw אלהים into the second clause (ὁ θεὸς χάριν... δώσει), so that ה' in b. should be construed with לא ימנע.

entries.emendation: הֶאָסַפְתָּ (interrogative, ה drawn from the preceding סלה); הֱשִׁיבוֹתָ → הֵשַׁבְתָּ
entries.note: Taken categorically (as a statement) the interpreters create a contradiction with v.5b and הפר כעסך (v.7). One is compelled to take v.4 as a question: draw the ה of the preceding סלה to אספת, giving הֶאָסַפְתָּ. This is confirmed by השיבות itself — the Hiphil is never used in this construction, only the Kal (שוב מחרון אפך); so leg. הֵשַׁבְתָּ מֵחֲרוֹן.
הלא אתה would be superfluous; leg. עתה 'now' statt אתה (a frequent confusion of עתה/אתה; cf. Monatschrift 1880, p.1ff.).

entries.emendation: supply/restore בִּי: מַה יְדַבֵּר בִּי הָאֵל (per LXX)
entries.note: From here the psalm answers the desperate question of the opening, though the transition is a little obscured; sense is eased by the LXX's preserved addition τί λαλήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ ὁ θεός = מה ידבר בי האל. What the psalmist proclaims is not his own thought (מלבו) but divinely inspired, as if רוח ה׳ דבר בי, answering the opening complaint. Accordingly vv.10ff. are spoken in God's name but in the third person, not as direct quotation.

entries.mt: צֶדֶק לְפָנָיו יְהַלֵּךְ וְיָשֵׂם לְדֶרֶךְ פְּעָמָיו
entries.note: Doubtful whether this verse refers to God or to the people. Statt לדרך Pesch. has לארעא = לארץ, but that reading rather obscures the sense than clarifies it.
b. is too short; supply כי ידעתי, as Ps 56:10.

יחד לבבי, 'unite my heart', yields no graspable sense; LXX εὐφρανθήτω ἡ καρδία μου and Pesch. likewise point (from חדה 'to rejoice') to an apocopated imperfect: 'let my heart rejoice to fear Thy name'.
